meta.title: Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) in Algeria — BTH Expert
meta.description: Certified consultancy for conducting Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA) in Algeria. Reports compliant with Ministry of Environment requirements. Based in Oran.

hero.heading: Environmental Impact Assessment
hero.subheading: The EIA is the regulatory document that assesses a project's impacts on its natural, human and socio-economic environment. It is mandatory for classified installations where the nomenclature requires it and for the projects listed by Executive Decree No. 07-145, as amended in 2018 and 2019.

why.heading: Who is concerned?
why.description: Any industrial, mining, agricultural, or infrastructure project owner whose project appears on the list of works subject to EIE is legally required to produce this study prior to obtaining their construction or operating permit.

steps.title: Initial site assessment
steps.description: Inventory of environmental components: physical, biological, human, and landscape settings. Data collected on-site and from secondary sources.

steps.title: Impact analysis
steps.description: Identification, qualification, and prioritization of direct and indirect impacts of the project on environmental components. Temporary and permanent impacts.

steps.title: Mitigation measures
steps.description: Definition of suppression, reduction, and compensation measures for significant impacts. Each measure is costed and scheduled.

steps.title: Monitoring program
steps.description: Environmental monitoring indicators, control frequency, alert thresholds, and reporting procedures to the Ministry of Environment.

deliverable.heading: Deliverable
deliverable.description: An EIA report structured according to Article 6 of Decree 07-145, with its descriptive report for the public inquiry, ready for filing with the wali in fourteen paper copies and two digital copies.

faq.q: When is an Environmental Impact Assessment mandatory?
faq.a: As soon as the nomenclature of classified installations (Decree 07-144) requires it for your heading, or your project appears on the list annexed to Executive Decree No. 07-145. The EIA conditions the building or operating permit.

faq.q: How long does an EIE take?
faq.a: Depending on the scale and sensitivity of the site, it can take from a few weeks to several months. We define the timeline from the initial consultation.

faq.q: Who validates the final report?
faq.a: The minister in charge of the environment for the impact assessment, the wali for the impact notice (Article 18 of Decree 07-145). The decision is notified to the project owner by the wali.

cta.heading: Does your project require an EIE?
cta.description: Send us the technical details of your project. We assess the scope of the study and provide you with a quote within 48 hours.

meta.title: Hazard Study (EDD) for Classified Establishments — BTH Expert
meta.description: Certified consultancy for conducting Hazard Studies (EDD) in Algeria: major risk analysis, accident scenarios, effect zones, and prevention plans. Based in Oran.

hero.heading: Hazard Study
hero.subheading: The Hazard Study identifies and characterizes the risks of major accidents at an industrial facility, assesses their consequences, and defines control measures. It is required for classified establishments subject to authorization.

why.heading: Who is concerned?
why.description: Any operator of a classified installation for environmental protection subject to authorization (hydrocarbon storage, petrochemical units, hazardous product depots, pressure equipment) must produce a Hazard Study before commissioning and revise it after each substantial modification.

steps.title: Description & Environment
steps.description: Characterization of the installation, products, processes, and environmental vulnerability: populations, sensitive areas, and potential domino effects.

steps.title: Hazard Identification
steps.description: Systematic analysis of hazard potentials using recognized methods (APR, HAZOP), leveraging accident history feedback and cataloguing feared scenarios.

steps.title: Risk Analysis & Modelling
steps.description: Quantification of major scenarios: thermal, overpressure, and toxic effects, calculation of effect zones, and mapping of isolation distances.

steps.title: Risk Control
steps.description: Definition of prevention and protection barriers, and of the elements of the internal intervention plan required by Executive Decree 25-63 of 28 January 2025.

deliverable.heading: Deliverable
deliverable.description: A Hazard Study report compliant with the Algerian regulatory framework, incorporating the effect zone mapping and risk control plan, ready for submission to the competent authorities.

faq.q: Is my installation concerned?
faq.a: Any classified installation subject to authorization: hydrocarbon storage, petrochemical units, hazardous product depots, pressure equipment.

faq.q: What does the Hazard Study contain?
faq.a: Hazard identification, modelling of major scenarios (thermal, overpressure, and toxic effects), effect zone mapping, and risk control plan.

faq.q: Does it need to be revised?
faq.a: Yes, after each substantial modification to the installation, processes, or products in use.

cta.heading: Does your installation require an EDD?
cta.description: Send us the characteristics of your installation and processes. We will assess the scope of the study and provide you with a quote within 48 hours.

meta.title: HSE Audit & Regulatory Compliance — BTH Expert
meta.description: Hygiene, safety and environment (HSE) audit and regulatory compliance assessment for industrial sites in Algeria. Gap identification and prioritized action plan. Certified consultancy in Oran.

hero.heading: HSE Audit & Compliance
hero.subheading: The HSE Audit establishes the compliance status of a site with respect to hygiene, safety and environmental requirements. It highlights regulatory gaps and prioritizes the corrective actions to be taken.

why.heading: Who is concerned?
why.description: Any industrial or tertiary site seeking to secure its regulatory compliance, prepare for an inspection, initiate an ISO 14001 / 45001 approach, or manage its HSE risks before an acquisition, an expansion, or a certification.

steps.title: Document Review
steps.description: Analysis of existing permits, orders, registers and procedures against the regulatory obligations applicable to the site.

steps.title: Site Visit
steps.description: Inspection of facilities, workstations and safety devices; interviews with managers and observation of actual practices.

steps.title: Gap Analysis
steps.description: Comparison of existing conditions against legal and normative requirements, and assessment of the criticality of each identified gap.

steps.title: Prioritized Action Plan
steps.description: Costed and scheduled recommendations, ranked by risk level and regulatory deadline.

deliverable.heading: Deliverable
deliverable.description: A comprehensive HSE Audit report: regulatory compliance grid, gap register and prioritized action plan, a steering tool for bringing the site into compliance.

faq.q: When should an HSE Audit be carried out?
faq.a: Before an inspection, an ISO certification, an acquisition or an expansion, or simply to durably secure your compliance.

faq.q: What is the deliverable?
faq.a: A regulatory compliance grid, a gap register and an action plan prioritized by risk level.

faq.q: Do you carry out on-site assessments?
faq.a: Yes. Document review followed by a site visit, interviews and observation of actual practices.

cta.heading: Need an HSE Audit?
cta.description: Tell us about your site and your compliance objectives. We define the audit scope and provide you with a proposal within 48 hours.

meta.title: Environmental Management Plan (PGE) — BTH Expert

hero.heading: Environmental Management Plan
hero.subheading: The Environmental Management Plan translates the commitments of the impact assessment into concrete measures: it organises the mitigation, surveillance, and monitoring of a project's effects, from the construction phase through to operation.

why.heading: Who is concerned?
why.description: Any project developer whose impact assessment has prescribed mitigation and monitoring measures, as well as operators required to demonstrate the proper implementation of their environmental commitments to the authorities.

steps.title: Commitment scoping
steps.description: Review of mitigation and compensation measures from the impact assessment and translation into assigned, scheduled operational actions.

steps.title: Monitoring programme
steps.description: Definition of indicators, parameters to be measured, control frequencies, and alert thresholds for each environmental component.

steps.title: Follow-up framework
steps.description: Organisation of responsibilities, reporting procedures, and control arrangements during both the construction and operational phases.

steps.title: Continuous improvement
steps.description: Review mechanisms, updating of measures, and handling of non-conformities throughout the entire life of the project.

deliverable.heading: Deliverable
deliverable.description: A fully operational Environmental Management Plan: a measures matrix, a monitoring and follow-up programme, indicators and a reporting template, ready to be used directly by the project teams.

faq.q: What is a PGE used for?
faq.a: It translates the commitments of the impact assessment into concrete measures: mitigation, surveillance, and monitoring throughout the entire project lifecycle.

faq.q: Who is concerned?
faq.a: Any project developer whose impact assessment has prescribed monitoring measures, and operators required to demonstrate their commitments.

faq.q: What does the deliverable contain?
faq.a: A measures matrix, a monitoring programme, indicators, and a reporting template ready to be used by your teams.

cta.heading: Structure your environmental monitoring?
cta.description: Share the requirements of your impact assessment with us. We will build a management plan tailored to your project and provide you with a quote within 48 hours.

list.title: Industry & Petrochemicals
list.tagline: Refining, cement plants, metallurgy and surface treatments: processes with high impact and hazard potential.
list.intro: Industrial and petrochemical sites concentrate the most demanding environmental and safety challenges: atmospheric and aqueous discharges, storage of hazardous products, and major accident risks. BTH Expert supports these installations from impact assessment through to risk management.

enjeux.title: Classified installations
enjeux.description: Environmental Impact Assessments and Hazard Studies for establishments subject to authorisation.

enjeux.title: Discharges & emissions
enjeux.description: Characterisation and reduction of atmospheric and aqueous discharges and special waste.

enjeux.title: Major accident risk
enjeux.description: Scenarios, effect zones and prevention plans for high-risk processes.

list.nomenclatureNote: Refining, petrochemicals, cement works, metallurgy and surface treatment fall under the 'substances' headings (1100 to 1800: very toxic, toxic, flammable, oxidising, corrosive) and the 'materials, ores and metals' (2500) and 'chemicals, rubber' (2600) families of the nomenclature. Above the quantity or capacity thresholds, the regime moves from wali authorisation to ministerial authorisation, with an impact assessment and a hazard study required, and a public-inquiry posting radius of several kilometres.

textes.note: The nomenclature classifies your site: heading by heading it sets the competent authority, the posting radius and the required studies. An industrial complex often falls under several headings; the most demanding one sets the category.

A 1st or 2nd category classified establishment in most cases: impact assessment and hazard study approved before the application, prior agreement for creation within fifteen days before any works, compliance visit, authorisation by joint ministerial order or by the wali.
Content of the impact assessment (Article 6), filing with the wali in fourteen copies, fifteen-day public inquiry except in industrial zones, approval by the minister in charge of the environment.

Vulnerability study before set-up (Article 75) and internal intervention plan (Article 76); specific intervention plan when the hazard study concludes that effects may extend beyond the site (Decree 25-63).
The studies must be signed by an accredited consultancy; a copy of the accreditation decision has been part of the impact assessment since 2018.

parcours.title: Classify each installation
parcours.description: Match processes, storage and capacities against the nomenclature headings; derive the establishment's category, the competent authority and the posting radius. Deliverable: classification note.

parcours.title: Environmental impact assessment
parcours.description: Baseline with surveys, impacts of air and water discharges and special waste, costed measures, environmental management plan. Approval by the minister in charge of the environment after the public inquiry.

parcours.title: Hazard study
parcours.description: Major-accident scenarios, thermal, overpressure and toxic effect zones, control measures. Filed in eight copies, examined by the interministerial or wilaya commission, approval signed by the ministers or the wali.

parcours.title: Application for an operating permit
parcours.description: File submitted to the wali with both approved studies; prior agreement for creation within fifteen days; works; compliance visit; permit within three months with its prescriptions.

parcours.title: Management plan and internal intervention plan
parcours.description: Implementation of the monitoring programme of the impact assessment and of the internal intervention plan approved by the wilaya commission, with at least two exercises a year.

parcours.title: HSE audit and updates
parcours.description: Periodic compliance audit; any extension, change of process or product requires a new application and an updated hazard study.

list.title: Energy & Hydrocarbons
list.tagline: Exploration, production, transport and storage of hydrocarbons, and energy production: strategic and sensitive infrastructure.
list.intro: The energy and hydrocarbons sector operates extensive and sensitive infrastructure, subject to a strict regulatory framework. BTH Expert intervenes across the entire chain, from production fields to transport and storage installations.

enjeux.title: Extensive sites
enjeux.description: Impact assessment across large footprints and varied environments.

enjeux.title: Installation safety
enjeux.description: Hazard Studies for storage, transport and processing units.

enjeux.title: Transition & efficiency
enjeux.description: Integration of energy challenges and renewable energies into projects.

list.nomenclatureNote: Hydrocarbon and gas depots and storage fall under the 'flammable' (1500, including flammable gases in 1510) and 'combustible' (1600) headings of the nomenclature, with an impact assessment and a hazard study from the first thresholds. Oil, gas or mineral exploration or extraction projects, hydrocarbon pipelines, wind farms (masts above 50 m and above 20 MW) and solar plants above 20 MW appear in Annex I of Decree 07-145; power lines above 30 kV in Annex II.

textes.note: Activities in the hydrocarbons domain follow a specific regime: their impact assessments remain governed by Executive Decree 08-312 of 5 October 2008 (Article 11 of Decree 18-255). Renewable energy and grid projects follow the common regime of the annexes revised in 2019.
For hydrocarbons, environmental accreditation is not enough: the consultancy must also be pre-qualified by the Hydrocarbons Regulatory Authority (Executive Decree 24-278 of 13 August 2024).
Storage, distribution and processing of hydrocarbons and gas: flammable and combustible headings, ministerial or wali authorisation depending on quantities, hazard study required.

The internal intervention plan is expressly required of operators of industrial installations and hydrocarbon pipelines (Article 76); pipelines and hydrocarbon installations are covered by a specific intervention plan (Article 4 of Decree 25-63).
Operating-permit regime, prior agreement, compliance visit and control by the wilaya commission for the sector's classified establishments.

parcours.title: Identify the applicable regime
parcours.description: Hydrocarbons-domain activity (Decree 08-312 regime and ARH pre-qualification) or energy and grid project (common regime); classification of storage and installations in the nomenclature.

parcours.title: Environmental impact assessment
parcours.description: Large footprints, varied environments, construction and operation phases; for pipelines and extraction sites, a full impact assessment under Annex I.

parcours.title: Hazard study
parcours.description: Fire, explosion, gas dispersion: scenarios, effect zones and control measures for storage, processing units and pipelines; approval by the competent commission.

parcours.title: Intervention plans
parcours.description: Mandatory internal intervention plan for hydrocarbon installations and pipelines, specific intervention plan set by order of the wali, approval by the wilaya commission within three months, regular exercises.

parcours.title: Operating permit
parcours.description: Prior agreement for creation, works, compliance visit, authorisation order with its technical prescriptions.

parcours.title: Monitoring and HSE audit
parcours.description: Monitoring programme, compliance audits, update of studies and plans after any accident, exercise or modification of the installation.

list.title: Infrastructure & Construction
list.tagline: Roads, civil engineering structures, business zones, buildings and developments: large-footprint structuring projects.
list.intro: Infrastructure and construction projects durably transform the territory. BTH Expert supports project owners and contractors in anticipating impacts, securing authorisations and organising environmental monitoring of construction sites.

enjeux.title: Footprint & territory
enjeux.description: Assessment of impacts on natural environments, landscape and neighbouring populations.

enjeux.title: Construction phase
enjeux.description: Management plans and monitoring of nuisances during the works phase.

enjeux.title: Authorisations
enjeux.description: Compilation of regulatory files required to obtain permits.

list.nomenclatureNote: Major works are not in the nomenclature but in the annexes of Decree 07-145 revised in 2019: motorways, airports, ports, dams, warehouses and distribution centres of 20,000 m² and more require an impact assessment; business parks and industrial zones, car parks of more than 100 vehicles, urban subdivisions above 10 ha and power lines above 30 kV require a notice. Site installations (concrete plants, asphalt plants, quarries and mineral processing, headings 2500) are classified installations.

textes.note: Annex I or II decides between an assessment and a notice for a structure; projects located in industrial zones, business parks or port zones already subject to a public inquiry are exempt (Article 9).

Article 15: any development, infrastructure or planning project likely to affect the environment is subject beforehand to an assessment or a notice; Article 22: carried out by an accredited consultancy.
Quarries, mineral processing, concrete plants and asphalt plants are classified installations: regime and studies according to the heading, authorisation before operation.
For classified site installations: prior agreement for creation before works, declaration sixty days before operation for the 4th category, new application in case of transfer.
Risk-prevention plans and safety perimeters around hazardous installations condition the siting of structures; every industrial installation is subject to a vulnerability study (Article 75).

parcours.title: Assessment or notice?
parcours.description: Read Annexes I and II of Decree 07-145 (2019 version) with the surface, capacity and power thresholds; classify site installations separately in the nomenclature.

parcours.title: Impact assessment or notice
parcours.description: Footprint, environments crossed, landscape, neighbouring populations, construction and operation phases, cumulative effects; costed measures and environmental management plan.

parcours.title: Public inquiry and approval
parcours.description: Fifteen days of posting and register led by an inquiry commissioner, written reply within ten days, approval by the minister (assessment) or the wali (notice). No work before approval.

parcours.title: Authorisation of site installations
parcours.description: Concrete plants, asphalt, quarries: prior agreement, compliance visit, authorisation or declaration depending on the category.

parcours.title: Environmental management plan during works
parcours.description: Monitoring of nuisances (dust, noise, site water, waste), indicators and reporting provided for in the impact assessment.

parcours.title: Restoration and closure
parcours.description: Dismantling of site installations, restoration of the site as provided in the impact assessment, declaration of definitive shutdown for classified installations.

list.title: Agriculture & Hydraulics
list.tagline: Irrigated perimeters, dams, wastewater treatment plants and agro-industrial projects: water resources at the heart of the challenges.
list.intro: Agriculture and hydraulics mobilise water resources and soils across large areas. BTH Expert assesses impacts, optimises water management and supports the regulatory compliance of agro-industrial and hydraulic projects.

enjeux.title: Water resources
enjeux.description: Preservation of water quality and availability for ecosystems and uses.

enjeux.title: Soils & environments
enjeux.description: Assessment of effects on soils, biodiversity and sensitive ecosystems.

enjeux.title: Treatment & discharges
enjeux.description: Design and monitoring of treatment systems and discharge management devices.

list.nomenclatureNote: Livestock farms (heading 2110), slaughterhouses (2210) and agri-food units (2200), desalination plants (2724) and water and waste treatment installations (2700) are classified installations. Dams require an impact assessment under Annex I of Decree 07-145; water supply for more than 10,000 inhabitants, hill reservoirs and hydraulic works of more than 500 m² require a notice (Annex II).

textes.note: Dams in Annex I; water supply, hill reservoirs, embankments and rock armouring in Annex II; study content focused on water resources, soils and biodiversity, with an environmental management plan.
Livestock, slaughterhouses, agri-food, desalination and water treatment are classified: regime, posting radius and required studies heading by heading.

For classified units: impact assessment or notice and, depending on the heading, hazard study or report on hazardous products, then prior agreement and operating permit; mandatory report on wastewater and emissions (Article 8).
Surface-water mobilisation works whose risk study concludes that effects may extend beyond the structure are covered by a specific intervention plan (Article 4 of Decree 25-63).
Principles of Article 3 (non-degradation of natural resources, prevention at source) and the assessment or notice obligation of Article 15 for hydro-agricultural developments.

parcours.title: Identify the applicable text
parcours.description: Hydraulic structure (annexes of Decree 07-145) or classified unit (nomenclature): the starting point differs, and some projects combine both.

parcours.title: Impact assessment or notice
parcours.description: Water-resource balance, soil quality, biodiversity and sensitive ecosystems, discharges and effluents; costed measures and environmental management plan.

parcours.title: Hazard study or report on hazardous products
parcours.description: Required where the heading provides for it (chemical storage, desalination, refrigeration ammonia); otherwise a report on the hazardous products held.

parcours.title: Public inquiry and approval
parcours.description: Filing with the wali, fifteen-day inquiry, opinions of the services, approval by the minister or the wali; prior agreement for creation for classified units.

parcours.title: Environmental management plan and water monitoring
parcours.description: Quality and abstraction indicators, monitoring of treatment systems and discharges, reporting to the environment services.

parcours.title: Specific intervention plan and audits
parcours.description: For hazardous hydraulic structures, specific intervention plan approved by the wilaya commission; compliance audits for agri-industrial units.

items.q: Which projects require an environmental impact assessment in Algeria?
items.a: Two sources say so: the nomenclature of classified installations (Executive Decree 07-144), which indicates heading by heading whether an impact assessment or notice is required, and the lists annexed to Decree 07-145 (revised in 2019) for other projects, such as infrastructure, developments or energy. In both cases the study must be approved before any building or operating permit.

items.q: What is the average timeframe to obtain an environmental authorization?
items.a: The texts frame each step: one month of examination by the environment services, a fifteen-day public inquiry, one month for the technical services' opinion, ten days for the written reply. In practice, allow 2 to 6 months depending on the project and the wilaya, excluding the time needed to produce the study itself.

items.q: Does BTH Expert operate outside of Oran?
items.a: Yes. Based in Oran, we operate throughout Algeria, with a focus on western Algeria: Oran, Mostaganem, Tlemcen, Sidi Bel Abbès, Relizane, and neighboring wilayas.

items.q: What is a Ministry of Environment accreditation?
items.a: It is an accreditation issued by order of the minister in charge of the environment, under Executive Decree 23-324 of 6 September 2023, for five renewable years. Only an accredited consultancy can produce an admissible impact assessment or hazard study. BTH Expert is accredited.

items.title: Protection of the environment within the framework of sustainable development
items.officialTitle: Law No. 03-10 of 19 July 2003 on the protection of the environment within the framework of sustainable development, published in Official Journal No. 43 of 20 July 2003, as amended
items.summary: Algeria's framework environmental law. It sets the principles (Article 3), subjects projects to an impact assessment or notice (Articles 15 and 16), defines classified establishments and their authorisation regimes (Articles 18 to 25) and reserves the studies to accredited consultancies (Article 22).
items.homeLine: The founding text: any project likely to affect the environment requires an impact assessment or notice (Art. 15), and classified establishments require authorisation or declaration (Art. 19).

sections.heading: What the law requires
list: Article 15: development projects, infrastructure, fixed installations, plants and development works which, through their direct or indirect effects on the environment, are subject beforehand to an impact assessment or an impact notice, as the case may be.

Article 16: the minimum content of the impact assessment (description of the activity, baseline of the site, potential impact on the environment and health with alternative solutions, effects on cultural heritage and socio-economic conditions, mitigation measures); the lists of projects subject to an assessment or a notice are set by regulation.

Articles 18 and 19: plants, workshops, worksites, quarries, mines and any installation presenting dangers to health, safety, agriculture, ecosystems or neighbourhood amenity are classified installations, subject to authorisation by the minister in charge of the environment, the wali or the president of the municipal assembly; those requiring neither an assessment nor a notice fall under a declaration to the president of the municipal assembly.
Article 21: the authorisation is preceded by an impact assessment or notice, a public inquiry and a study of the project's dangers and effects, and is granted only once these steps are completed.

Article 22: the impact assessment or notice is carried out, at the project owner's expense, by consultancies, expert offices or consulting offices accredited by the ministry in charge of the environment.
Article 25: where an installation, even outside the nomenclature, presents serious dangers, the wali serves formal notice on the operator; failing compliance, operation is suspended.

sections.heading: The principles of Article 3
paragraphs: The law states the principles guiding every decision: preservation of biological diversity, non-degradation of natural resources, substitution, integration, preventive action and correction as a priority at source, precaution, polluter pays, public information and participation. A well-built impact assessment refers to them explicitly.

sections.heading: Who is concerned
list: manufacturers, whatever the size of the unit, as soon as the activity is classified;
infrastructure owners: roads, business parks, hydraulic works;
quarry operators and mining projects;
large agricultural and hydraulic projects (irrigated perimeters, dams, treatment plants);
local authorities for their facilities (landfills, wastewater plants).

sections.heading: What it changes for your project
paragraphs: The building or operating permit cannot be issued before the impact assessment is approved. Starting the study at the design stage, not at filing time, avoids the most common blockage: a construction schedule waiting for an approval.

Law 03-10 is not read alone. Project lists, study contents and procedures are set by its implementing decrees: 07-145 for impact assessments (amended in 2018 and 2019), 06-198 for classified establishments (amended in 2022) and 07-144 for the nomenclature.

faq.q: Does Law 03-10 apply to an existing installation?
faq.a: Yes. Article 24 refers existing installations to regulation, and Decree 06-198, as amended in 2022, requires any existing establishment without authorisation to regularise its situation after approval of an environmental audit and a hazard study.

faq.q: Who approves the impact assessment?
faq.a: Decree 07-145 (Article 18) specifies it: the impact assessment is approved by the minister in charge of the environment, the impact notice by the territorially competent wali. The decision is notified to the project owner by the wali.

items.metaDescription: Sheet checked against OJ No. 43 of 20 July 2003: principles (Art. 3), impact assessment or notice (Arts. 15-16), classified establishments and authorisation (Arts. 18-21), accredited consultancies (Art. 22). What Law 03-10 changes for your project.

items.title: Environmental impact assessments and notices
items.officialTitle: Executive Decree No. 07-145 of 19 May 2007 determining the scope, content and approval procedure of environmental impact assessments and notices (OJ No. 34 of 22 May 2007), as amended by Executive Decree No. 18-255 of 9 October 2018 (OJ No. 62 of 17 October 2018) and Executive Decree No. 19-241 of 8 September 2019 (OJ No. 54 of 8 September 2019)
items.summary: The text that says whether your project requires an impact assessment or an impact notice, what the report must contain, how the wilaya reviews it (filing, examination, fifteen-day public inquiry, opinions of the services) and who approves it: the minister for the assessment, the wali for the notice.
items.homeLine: Sets the projects subject to an assessment or a notice, the content of the report and its review: filing with the wali, examination within one month, fifteen-day public inquiry, approval by the minister (assessment) or the wali (notice).

sections.heading: Assessment or notice: two sources to check
paragraphs: Article 3 of the decree sets the rule: an assessment or notice is required, on the one hand, for classified installations where the nomenclature of Decree 07-144 demands it (the nomenclature has an 'impact assessment' column and an 'impact notice' column for each heading), and on the other hand for the projects listed in the annexes of Decree 07-145. Those annexes were entirely replaced by Decree 19-241 of 2019.
list: Annex I (impact assessment), examples from the text: tourist developments of 10 hectares and more, motorways, airports, ports, dams, warehouses and distribution centres of 20,000 m² and more, developments in wetlands, hydrocarbon pipelines, exploration or extraction of oil, gas or minerals, railway lines, hospitals of 500 beds and more, wind farms above 20 MW, solar plants above 20 MW.

Annex II (impact notice), examples: development of business parks and industrial zones, car parks of more than 100 vehicles, power lines above 30 kV, water supply for more than 10,000 inhabitants, shopping centres of 5,000 m² and more, hospitals of 60 to 500 beds.
sections.after: A plant, a cement works or a hydrocarbon depot do not appear in these annexes: their impact-assessment obligation comes from the nomenclature of classified installations. Classification is therefore always checked heading by heading.

sections.heading: Content of the report (Article 6, 2018 wording)
list: presentation of the project owner and of the consultancy, with a copy of the accreditation decision issued by the minister in charge of the environment;
analysis of the project's alternatives and variants, justifying the choices made on economic, technological and environmental grounds;
delimitation of the study area according to the posting radius of the nomenclature (classified installations) or within a radius of at most 3 km (annex projects);
detailed description of the site's baseline (natural resources, biodiversity, land, marine or water areas, air quality), with a 1:2,500 location plan and a 1:200 site plan;
description of the project phases (construction, operation, post-operation) and estimate of residues, emissions and nuisances;
assessment of foreseeable direct and indirect impacts in the short, medium and long term, and cumulative effects;
measures planned to eliminate, reduce or offset harmful consequences, with their financial implications;
detailed environmental management plan with an implementation schedule;
descriptive report of the project, prepared by the consultancy and made available to the public during the inquiry.
sections.after: The assessment is prepared by a consultancy accredited by the minister in charge of the environment (Article 4, referring to Article 22 of Law 03-10; accreditation conditions set by Decree 23-324).

sections.heading: Procedure and regulatory deadlines
list: filing by the project owner with the territorially competent wali, in fourteen paper copies and two digital copies (Article 7);

examination of the content by the environment services, referred by the wali, within one month; additional information to be provided within two months, failing which the assessment is rejected unless a reasoned extension is requested (Article 8);

after preliminary examination and acceptance, opening of the public inquiry by order of the wali; projects located in industrial zones, business parks, port zones, bonded zones and offshore projects already subject to a public inquiry are exempt (Article 9);

posting of the order at the wilaya and the municipalities concerned and on site, and publication in two national dailies at the project owner's expense; inquiry duration: fifteen days at most from posting; numbered and initialled register (Article 10);
inquiry commissioner appointed by the wali, who oversees posting, the register and additional checks, then submits a report (Articles 12 to 14);
opinions of the technical services, referred as soon as the inquiry opens, within one month; after one reminder, silence counts as a favourable opinion (Article 17);
the project owner's written reply to the opinions collected, within ten days (Article 15);
transmission of the complete file to the minister in charge of the environment for the impact assessment, or to the environment services for the notice (Article 16);
approval of the impact assessment by the minister in charge of the environment and of the notice by the wali; reasoned rejection; notification by the wali (Article 18);
in case of rejection, administrative appeal to the minister in charge of the environment, without prejudice to judicial remedies (Article 19).

sections.heading: Three rules not to forget
list: no construction work may start before approval of the assessment or notice (Article 21);
any change in the size of installations, capacity or processes after filing requires a new assessment or notice (Article 5);
approval of the assessment for an extension does not replace the operating permit of the existing establishment (Article 5, paragraph added in 2018).

sections.heading: Timeframes to plan for in practice
paragraphs: Since 2018 the decree no longer sets an overall decision deadline after the inquiry; it frames each step: one month of examination, two months for additional information, fifteen days of inquiry, one month for the services' opinions, ten days for the reply. In practice, allow two to six months depending on the wilaya and the quality of the file, excluding the time needed to produce the study itself. Requests for additional information are the first cause of slippage, and they are prevented at the writing stage.

faq.q: Can works start during the review?
faq.a: No. Article 21 prohibits it: no construction work may start before approval of the impact assessment or notice.

faq.q: Who can carry out the impact assessment?
faq.a: A consultancy accredited by the minister in charge of the environment (Article 4). Since 2018, a copy of the accreditation decision is part of the mandatory content of the assessment. BTH Expert holds this accreditation.

faq.q: Is the study made public?
faq.a: Yes, during the public inquiry: the order is posted and published in two national dailies, a descriptive report of the project is made available to the public, and anyone may ask to consult the study and then has fifteen days to submit observations (Article 11).

faq.q: Do hydrocarbon projects follow the same procedure?
faq.a: No. Impact assessments for hydrocarbon activities remain governed by Executive Decree 08-312 of 5 October 2008 (Article 11 of Decree 18-255), and consultancies must also be pre-qualified by the Hydrocarbons Regulatory Authority (Executive Decree 24-278 of 13 August 2024).

items.title: Classified establishments for environmental protection
items.officialTitle: Executive Decree No. 06-198 of 31 May 2006 defining the regulations applicable to classified establishments for environmental protection (OJ No. 37 of 4 June 2006), as amended by Executive Decree No. 22-167 of 19 April 2022 (OJ No. 29 of 24 April 2022)
items.summary: The authorisation regime for classified establishments: four categories and three authorities, a prior agreement for creation before works, a compliance visit before the operating permit, and the hazard study that conditions the opening.
items.homeLine: Makes the operating permit of a classified establishment conditional on an approved impact assessment and an approved hazard study, a prior agreement for creation and a compliance visit, across four categories and three authorities.

meta.label: Authorities
meta.value: Minister · Wali or delegated wali · Municipal president

sections.heading: Four categories, three authorities (Article 3)
list: 1st category: establishment with at least one installation subject to ministerial authorisation; the operating permit is issued by joint order of the minister in charge of the environment and the minister concerned (Article 20);
2nd category: at least one installation subject to authorisation by the territorially competent wali or delegated wali (2022 wording);
3rd category: at least one installation subject to authorisation by the president of the municipal assembly;
4th category: at least one installation under the declaration regime with the president of the municipal assembly, filed at least sixty days before operation starts (Article 24).
sections.after: The regime of each installation (AM, AW, APAPC or D) is shown, heading by heading, in the nomenclature of Decree 07-144.

sections.heading: What precedes any application (Article 5)
paragraphs: Any application for an operating permit is preceded, according to the nomenclature:
list: by an impact assessment or notice prepared and approved under Decree 07-145;
by a hazard study prepared and approved under Decree 06-198;
by a public inquiry.

sections.heading: The file and the procedure (Articles 6 to 8, 2022 wording)
list: filing of the application with the wali, with the approved studies;
preliminary examination of the file by the wilaya commission for the control of classified establishments;

prior agreement decision for the creation of the classified establishment within fifteen days of filing: drawn up by the environment services and issued by the minister in charge of the environment (1st category) or by the wali, where applicable the delegated wali (2nd and 3rd categories), then notified to the project owner; it transcribes the prescriptions of the approval decisions of the impact assessment and the hazard study (Articles 16 and 17);
no construction work may start before the prior agreement is obtained (Article 18);
at the end of the works, site visit by the commission and compliance report (Article 19);
issue of the operating permit within three months of the project owner's request at the end of the works; the order sets the specific technical prescriptions (Articles 20 and 21).
sections.after: The file includes the project owner's identity, the nature and volume of activities with the nomenclature headings, processes, materials and products, a 1:25,000 or 1:50,000 map, a location plan at 1:2,500 or larger up to one tenth of the posting radius (100 m minimum), an overall plan at 1:200 or larger up to 35 m, a report on hazardous products and a report on wastewater, emissions and waste (Articles 8 and 9).

sections.heading: The hazard study (Articles 12 to 15)
paragraphs: It specifies the direct or indirect risks through which the activity endangers people, property and the environment, whether the cause is internal or external, and defines the technical measures to reduce the likelihood and effects of accidents and the organisational measures for their prevention and management. It is carried out at the project owner's expense by a consultancy accredited by the minister in charge of the environment.
list: general presentation of the project;

description of the immediate environment and of the neighbourhood potentially affected: physical data (geology, hydrology, meteorology, seismicity) and socio-economic data (population, housing, water points, communication routes, protected areas);
description of the project and its installations, products and materials, with plans;
identification of all risk factors, intrinsic and extrinsic;
analysis of risks and consequences: accidental events, rating by severity and likelihood, assessment method used;
analysis of potential impacts in the event of an accident on populations, the environment and the economy;
organisation of site safety, prevention of major accidents, safety management system and emergency resources.
sections.after: Its examination and approval rules are set by the interministerial order of 14 September 2014 (OJ No. 3 of 27 January 2015): filing with the wali in eight copies, transmission within five days to the interministerial commission (1st category) or the wilaya commission (2nd category), possible request for additional information within forty-five days of referral, fifteen days for the project owner to reply, approval or rejection decision signed jointly by the ministers in charge of the interior and the environment (1st category) or by the wali (2nd category), notified by the wali.

sections.heading: Control, modifications and existing establishments
list: where non-compliance is found, a report and a deadline for regularisation; failing that, suspension of the permit, then withdrawal if compliance is not achieved within six months (Article 23);
any conversion of activity, change of process, transformation of equipment, extension or transfer requires a new application for authorisation or a new declaration (Articles 38 and 39);

an existing establishment without authorisation had to regularise its situation within one year of the 2022 decree; its application is preceded by the approval of an environmental audit and of the hazard study, the file is filed in two paper copies and fourteen electronic copies, and the commission visits the site within ten days (Articles 44 and 44 bis).

faq.q: Does an existing workshop need to apply for authorisation?
faq.a: Yes, if its activity appears in the nomenclature. Since 2022, the regularisation of an existing establishment first requires the approval of an environmental audit and a hazard study, then a compliance visit by the wilaya commission (Article 44 bis).

faq.q: What is the difference between an impact assessment and a hazard study?
faq.a: The impact assessment covers the installation's effects on the environment in normal operation (Decree 07-145). The hazard study covers accident risks and their control (Articles 12 to 15 of Decree 06-198). Both, once approved, precede the application for an operating permit (Article 5).

faq.q: When can works start?
faq.a: After the prior agreement decision for creation, issued within fifteen days of filing the complete file (Articles 6 and 18). The operating permit itself is issued only after the compliance visit at the end of the works (Article 19).

items.title: Nomenclature of classified installations
items.officialTitle: Executive Decree No. 07-144 of 19 May 2007 setting the nomenclature of classified installations for environmental protection (OJ No. 34 of 22 May 2007)
items.summary: The list of classified activities: for each heading, the authorisation or declaration regime, the posting radius of the public inquiry and the documents required (impact assessment, hazard study, impact notice, report on hazardous products).
items.homeLine: Assigns a heading to each activity and sets, for each, the regime (ministerial, wali or municipal authorisation, or declaration), the posting radius of the public inquiry and the required studies.

sections.heading: What the nomenclature contains (Article 2)
list: a four-digit heading number: the first digit designates the substance or activity, the second the hazard category (very toxic, toxic, flammable, oxidising, explosive, corrosive, combustible) or the branch of activity, the last two the type of activity;
the designation of the activity and, most often, thresholds of quantity, capacity or power;
the applicable regime, in accordance with Decree 06-198: AM (ministerial authorisation), AW (wali authorisation), APAPC (authorisation by the president of the municipal assembly) or D (declaration);
the posting radius, in kilometres: minimum posting radius of the notice opening the public inquiry, to inform the population within the siting perimeter;
the documents to attach to the authorisation application: impact assessment, hazard study, impact notice and report on hazardous products, depending on the heading.
sections.after: Example read in the nomenclature: heading 1110, industrial manufacture of very toxic substances, ministerial authorisation from 20 tonnes and wali authorisation below, 3 km posting radius, impact assessment and hazard study required in both cases.

sections.heading: Families of activities covered
list: substances: very toxic, toxic, oxidising, explosive, flammable, combustible, corrosive (headings 1100 to 1800);
livestock and agricultural activities, agri-food, textiles, hides and skins;
wood, paper, cardboard, printing; materials, ores and metals; chemicals and rubber;
waste and water treatment, including desalination plants; aquaculture and fishing;
miscellaneous activities: battery charging workshops, application of paints and varnishes, etc. (headings 2100 to 2900).

sections.heading: What it changes for your project
paragraphs: The classification conditions everything else: the authority issuing the permit, the procedure, the need for an impact assessment or a notice, the hazard-study requirement and the extent of the public inquiry. A single site often falls under several headings; the most demanding one sets the establishment's category. A classification error upstream is paid for at filing, through a rejection or a request for additional documents.

faq.q: How do I find my installation's category?
faq.a: By matching each activity on the site against the nomenclature headings and their thresholds, then reading the regime indicated (AM, AW, APAPC, D). It is the first step of an engagement, formalised in a classification note.

faq.q: Does a capacity increase change the category?
faq.a: It can: above a threshold, the heading moves for example from wali authorisation to ministerial authorisation. Any extension in any case requires a new application for authorisation (Article 38 of Decree 06-198).

items.title: Prevention, response and reduction of disaster risks
items.officialTitle: Law No. 24-04 of 26 February 2024 laying down the rules for the prevention, response and reduction of disaster risks within the framework of sustainable development (OJ No. 16 of 6 March 2024), repealing Law No. 04-20 of 25 December 2004; implementing text: Executive Decree No. 25-63 of 28 January 2025 (OJ No. 7 of 5 February 2025)
items.summary: The law that has replaced the former Law 04-20 on major risks since 2024. For an industrial operator it requires a vulnerability study before set-up (Article 75) and an internal intervention plan (Article 76), detailed by Decree 25-63 of 2025, which repeals the former decrees on intervention plans.
items.homeLine: Replaces Law 04-20 since 2024: every industrial installation is subject to a vulnerability study (Art. 75) and an internal intervention plan (Art. 76), governed by Decree 25-63 of 2025.

sections.heading: Risks covered (Article 3)
list: seismic, geological, flood, extreme climate and forest-fire risks;
industrial and energy risks;
space, radiological and nuclear risks;
risks to human, animal and plant health; risks of air, marine and water pollution;
risks of large human gatherings, desertification, drought, coastal erosion and sea-level rise.

sections.heading: Industrial operator obligations (Articles 73 to 76)
list: Article 75: every industrial installation must, before its set-up and operation, undergo a vulnerability study to disaster risks;

Article 76: operators of industrial installations and of hydrocarbon pipelines must draw up an internal intervention plan defining the prevention measures, alarm and alert systems, related technical studies, the resources mobilised and the procedures to implement in the event of a disaster;

Articles 73 and 74: specific intervention plans, established by regulation, protect industrial installations and structures; they analyse the risks, provide for alert arrangements and inform citizens.

sections.heading: Decree 25-63: specific and internal intervention plans
paragraphs: Issued under Articles 73 and 76, it sets the conditions for drawing up, implementing and managing both plans and repeals Decrees 15-71 (specific plans) and 09-335 (internal plans) (Article 29).
list: specific intervention plan: for classified establishments whose hazard study concludes that the effects of the risks may extend beyond the installation, hydraulic works, hydrocarbon and gas pipelines and hydrocarbon installations; the list is set by order of the wali (Articles 2 to 6);

internal intervention plan: for industrial installations and pipelines which, through danger of fire, explosion or toxic release, may create risks for workers, the population, property and the environment (Articles 7 and 8);

the plans are drawn up at the operator's expense, on the basis of a vulnerability study (specific plan) or a hazard study (internal plan), by State-accredited consultancies, following a template set by joint order (Articles 10 to 12);
approval by a wilaya commission chaired by the wali, which decides within three months, failing which the draft is deemed admissible (Articles 14 and 15);

simulation exercises: an annual programme for the specific plan, at least two exercises a year for the internal plan (Article 24); update after any accident, exercise or modification of the installation (Article 26);
installations in operation had one year to comply; a new installation may operate only after approval of its plans (Article 28).

sections.heading: Link with the hazard study
paragraphs: For an industrial site, the hazard study of Decree 06-198 is the technical basis of the internal intervention plan and determines whether a specific intervention plan is needed. A well-sized hazard study therefore speeds up the next procedure.

faq.q: Are the internal intervention plan and the hazard study the same thing?
faq.a: No. The hazard study analyses the risks and their consequences; the internal intervention plan sets the planning and management of response and rescue inside the installation in the event of an accident (Article 7 of Decree 25-63). The latter builds on the former.

faq.q: Is an internal plan drawn up under the former Decree 09-335 still valid?
faq.a: Decree 25-63 repeals Decree 09-335 and required installations in operation to comply with its provisions within one year (Articles 28 and 29). An existing plan must therefore be revised according to the new template and approved by the wilaya commission.

items.title: Accreditation of environmental consultancies
items.officialTitle: Executive Decree No. 23-324 of 6 September 2023 setting the conditions and procedures for practising as an environmental consultancy (OJ No. 61 of 17 September 2023)
items.summary: The text that says who is entitled to carry out your impact assessments, hazard studies and environmental audits: a consultancy accredited by order of the minister in charge of the environment, for five renewable years, classified in categories by staff and experience. A study signed by a non-accredited consultancy is inadmissible.
items.homeLine: Reserves impact assessments, hazard studies and environmental audits to consultancies accredited by order of the minister in charge of the environment, for five renewable years.

meta.label: Accreditation
meta.value: Order of the minister in charge of the environment (Art. 4)

meta.label: Categories
meta.value: A to E by staff and experience (Art. 22)

sections.heading: What the decree requires
list: the activity is regulated, registered in the trade register, and subject to an accreditation issued by order of the minister in charge of the environment after the opinion of a commission (Articles 2, 4 and 11);

natural person: Algerian nationality, university degree in the specialities of Annex 1, at least three years of experience in the environmental field; legal person: Algerian law, degree-holding manager, at least two degree-holding employees, three years of experience for the manager and staff (Article 6);
suitable premises and appropriate equipment and software (Article 7);
to specialise in impact assessments, hazard studies and environmental audits: training completed at the national conservatory for environmental training (Article 8);
examination of the file by the commission within forty-five days, notification within fifteen days; in case of rejection, appeal within one month, decided within twenty days (Articles 13 to 17);
accreditation granted for five renewable years, personal and non-transferable; renewal application at least forty-five days before expiry (Articles 18 to 20);
classification of consultancies into categories A to E according to the number of qualified staff and their years of experience (Article 22);

periodic control by the ministry; temporary (six months at most) or permanent withdrawal of accreditation in case of breach (Articles 24 to 27); existing consultancies had twelve months to comply (Article 31).

sections.heading: Why it concerns you
paragraphs: Decree 07-145 (Article 4) and Decree 06-198 (Article 13) require the impact assessment and the hazard study to be prepared by an accredited consultancy, and since 2018 a copy of the accreditation decision is a mandatory part of the impact assessment. A study signed by a consultancy without valid accreditation, or whose accreditation does not cover the type of study, is rejected. Before placing any order, ask for the accreditation order and check its expiry date and category.

For hydrocarbon-sector activities, environmental accreditation is not enough: the consultancy must also be pre-qualified by the Hydrocarbons Regulatory Authority (Executive Decree 24-278 of 13 August 2024, OJ No. 58 of 22 August 2024).

faq.q: Is BTH Expert accredited?
faq.a: Yes. BTH Expert is accredited by the ministry in charge of the environment to carry out impact assessments and hazard studies. The accreditation order is provided on request.

faq.q: Can a foreign consultancy carry out an impact assessment in Algeria?
faq.a: Accreditation is reserved for natural persons of Algerian nationality and legal persons under Algerian law (Articles 3 and 6). A foreign consultancy may, where relevant, support an accredited Algerian consultancy that signs the study.

items.title: Obtaining authorisation for a classified installation, step by step
items.officialTitle: Procedure guide: from the nomenclature to the operating permit, based on Decrees 07-144, 07-145, 06-198, 23-324 and 25-63 and the interministerial order of 14 September 2014
items.summary: From reading the nomenclature to the operating-permit order, the six steps of an industrial project's regulatory path in Algeria, with the deadlines set by the texts and what gains or loses months.

meta.label: Framed deadlines
meta.value: Inquiry 15 d · Prior agreement 15 d · Permit 3 months

sections.heading: Classify the installation
paragraphs: Match each activity on the site against the nomenclature headings (Decree 07-144) and their thresholds. For each heading the nomenclature gives the regime (ministerial, wali or municipal authorisation, or declaration), the posting radius and the required studies; the establishment's category follows (Article 3 of Decree 06-198). Deliverable: a classification note.

sections.heading: Determine the required studies
paragraphs: Impact assessment or impact notice according to the nomenclature and the annexes of Decree 07-145 revised in 2019; hazard study where the nomenclature requires it, or otherwise a report on hazardous products (Article 9 of Decree 06-198); vulnerability study and internal intervention plan under Law 24-04 and Decree 25-63. The impact assessment and the hazard study must be prepared by an accredited consultancy (Decree 23-324), whose accreditation decision is attached to the impact assessment.

sections.heading: Carry out the studies
paragraphs: For the impact assessment: alternatives, study area based on the posting radius, baseline with on-site surveys and plans at 1:2,500 and 1:200, direct, indirect and cumulative impacts, costed measures, environmental management plan with schedule, descriptive report for the public (Article 6 of Decree 07-145). For the hazard study: the seven elements of Article 14 of Decree 06-198, from risk factors to emergency resources. Allow a few weeks to several months depending on the project's scale.

sections.heading: File and have the studies approved
paragraphs: The impact assessment or notice is filed with the wali in fourteen paper copies and two digital copies; examination within one month, additional information within two months; public inquiry of fifteen days at most, except for projects in industrial zones, business parks, port or bonded zones; opinions of the technical services within one month; written reply within ten days; approval by the minister (assessment) or the wali (notice). The hazard study is filed in eight copies; the wali forwards it within five days to the interministerial or wilaya commission; additional information requested within forty-five days and provided within fifteen; decision signed by the ministers of the interior and the environment (1st category) or by the wali (2nd category).

sections.heading: Obtain the prior agreement, then build
paragraphs: The application for an operating permit, with the approved studies, is filed with the wali. The wilaya commission examines it and the prior agreement decision for creation is issued within fifteen days of filing, by the minister in charge of the environment (1st category) or by the wali or delegated wali (2nd and 3rd categories). No work may start before this agreement (Articles 6, 16 to 18 of Decree 06-198). This is also when the intervention plans are submitted to the wilaya commission, which decides within three months (Decree 25-63).

sections.heading: Obtain the operating permit and operate
paragraphs: At the end of the works, the commission visits the site and draws up a compliance report; the operating permit is issued within three months of the project owner's request, by joint order of the ministers (1st category), by the wali or delegated wali (2nd) or by the president of the municipal assembly (3rd), with its technical prescriptions. The obligation does not stop there: environmental management plan and monitoring, internal intervention plan exercises at least twice a year, compliance audits, and a new application for any modification, extension or transfer (Articles 19 to 23 and 38 of Decree 06-198).

sections.heading: What loses time
list: a wrong classification, sending the file to the wrong authority or omitting a study required by the nomenclature;
a desk-based baseline, with no on-site surveys or plans at the required scales;
mitigation measures that are neither costed nor scheduled in the environmental management plan;
a missing or unreadable descriptive report for the public;
an incomplete file, or a consultancy whose accreditation is not valid or does not cover the type of study.

faq.q: How long does the full procedure take?
faq.a: The texts frame each step (one month of examination, fifteen days of public inquiry, one month for opinions, ten days for the reply, fifteen days for the prior agreement, three months for the permit after the end of the works) but no longer set an overall deadline since 2018. In practice, allow two to six months of review after an admissible file, plus the time needed to produce the studies. A complete file at first filing is the main lever for shortening the delay.

faq.q: Is an accredited consultancy mandatory?
faq.a: Yes for the impact assessment (Article 4 of Decree 07-145) and the hazard study (Article 13 of Decree 06-198): only consultancies accredited by the minister in charge of the environment under Decree 23-324 are entitled to carry them out.
